title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-20
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs and commands for the intermittent 401 / 429 pattern we've been seeing in hosted-api during 03/18-03/20. Mostly notes to self, reproduce steps, hypotheses, and quick checks.

Observed behavior summary:
- Customers and internal smoke tests: sporadic 401s for a subset of requests; often followed by successful requests for same client after a short time.
- 429 spikes seen during bursts (traffic ramp, stress tests) even when global token usage well under quota.
- Patterns: 401s tend to show up immediately after key rotations or when requests route through a particular edge POP. 429s often include X-RateLimit headers that disagree with what clients expect.

Quick repro (local):
1) curl (valid key) sometimes returns 401: 
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxxx" \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hi"}'

   Response snippet (from repro on 2026-03-19 15:12:03 UTC):
   HTTP/2 401
   date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:12:03 GMT
   content-type: application/json
   content-length: 86
   x-request-id: r-4f3d2a
   {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"invalid or revoked api key"}

2) Immediately retrying same curl (same key) succeeds:
   HTTP/2 200
   x-request-id: r-4f3d2a-retry
   {"id":"resp_...","object":"text_completion","choices":[...]}

3) 429 example during burst test (2026-03-19 16:05:11 UTC):
   HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 16:05:11 GMT
   content-type: application/json
   retry-after: 2
   x-rate-limit-limit: 1000
   x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
   x-rate-limit-reset: 1710890713
   {"error":"Too many requests","message":"global concurrency limit exceeded"}

Immediate checks done:
- Verified key status in admin UI: key shows active, last rotation 2026-03-18 04:22 UTC. No explicit revocation.
- Checked KMS rotation logs: no rotations coincident with observed 401 spikes besides scheduled one on 03-18.
- Edge POP logs: some 401s concentrated on pop-us-west-2 (checked logs via splunk query: index=api prod POP=us-west-2 status=401).
- CDN cache: looked for cached auth responses — nothing obvious.
- SDK: internal SDK (node) had recent change to refresh token caching (PR #987). Reverted locally -> still see 401s in some runs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Short-lived propagation lag after key rotation: gateway caches JWT verification state (JWKS) and some POPs still using stale keys for a bit -> transient 401s. Evidence: clusters of 401s shortly after scheduled rotation on 03-18.
2) API Gateway per-POP token revocation cache mismatch: revocation/allowlist updates not propagated atomically, causing some POPs to think key is revoked.
3) Client-side intermittent header truncation when requests pass through proxy leading to missing Authorization header -> 401. Low evidence; would expect higher failure rate.
4) 429s are due to per-route concurrency caps and not the global quota; clients hit route-level burst limits. Evidence: x-rate-limit-* headers show remaining=0 even when account meter shows spare quota.
5) Bad retry logic in downstream retry library causing tight retry loops that trigger 429s.

Commands / queries to run next: (to collect evidence)
- Aggregated log query (splunk):
  index=api prod status=401 | stats count by pop, api_key_id, minute | sort -count
- Check JWKS caching TTL on each gateway instance: 
  curl https://edge-pop-{pop}.internal/config | jq .auth.jwks_ttl  (pop list: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1)
- Pause rotation in staging and run stress test to see if 401 frequency drops.
- Capture tcpdump from one of the affected POPs during a repro window to verify Authorization header bytes are intact.

Important log snippets saved (grabbed from edge-pop-us-west-2 logs):
- 2026-03-18T04:22:15Z EDGE AUTH key=k_12345 action=rotation scheduled_by=ops
- 2026-03-18T04:22:20Z EDGE AUTH key=k_12345 validation=ok pop=us-east-1
- 2026-03-18T04:22:21Z EDGE AUTH key=k_12345 validation=failed pop=us-west-2 reason="jwks-kid-mismatch"
- 2026-03-18T04:22:22Z EDGE AUTH key=k_12345 validation=ok pop=eu-west-1

Notes / intuition:
- The jwks-kid-mismatch line lines up with transient 401 reported by a customer right after rotation. That supports hypothesis #1/#2.
- 429s: need to differentiate between 'global token quota' reported by billing/usage and 'per-route concurrency' the runtime enforces. Past incident (INF-2389) shows route-level caps exist and were the culprit then.

Quick experiments performed:
- Increased jwks cache TTL to 0 on staging gateway (force fresh fetch every request) and ran 10k reqs over 2 minutes: 401s dropped to near 0, but latency increased. Suggests propagation/caching issue.
- Adjusted per-route concurrency from 500 -> 800 for stress tests: 429s reduced but still present at higher load -> suggests both concurrency and some bad client retry behavior.

Action items (next):
- [ ] Add temporary metric to monitor jwks_update_age by POP (ops ticket INF-4527).
- [ ] Add more detailed x-auth-diagnostics header on failures (include jwks-kid-check result). Low risk change to edge gateway.
- [ ] Reproduce in staging with controlled rotation and capture tcpdumps for Authorization header integrity check.
- [ ] Review SDK PR #987 for token caching edgecases; add logging around Authorization header composition.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra-net to check whether any proxies (envoy filters) might drop or truncate long Authorization headers.

Questions / unresolved:
- Why do some POPs report jwks-kid-mismatch while others succeed instantly? Propagation ordering? Race in rotation signal?
- Are there any rate limiters upstream (CDN) with independent counters contributing to 429s but not visible in our runtime metrics?

References / links:
- Jira: INF-4527 (auth rotation / 401 spikes)
- Prior incident: INF-2389 (rate-limit misconfiguration on /v1/generate)
- Slack thread: #infra-auth (pinned logs)

Notes to self: keep this doc messy — it's my scratchpad for ops pairing tomorrow with Michael. Will convert to playbook if we confirm root cause.

-- Lena
